description: KatLang is a domain-specific programming language for calculations. This package provides the core parser, evaluator, and semantic model.
releaseNotes: Internal architecture repair of the evaluator's plain/counted implementation pairs; no intended KatLang language-semantics change and no public API change. The authoritative Lean model and the C# runtime now share one ownership direction: wherever a plain/counted evaluator pair is semantically equivalent, the counted implementation is canonical and the plain implementation is its value projection, so plain/counted equivalence holds by construction instead of depending on two hand-maintained bodies staying in sync. In Lean, the counted expression dispatch now matches every AST variant explicitly (the numeric/string leaves and the unary/binary operator semantics moved into counted-owned arms), the former default arm that delegated counted evaluation back to the plain evaluator is gone, plain eval is a one-line total projection of counted eval, the user/conditional/resolved/expression-position call families project their counted twins exactly as the builtin and dot-call families already did, and the ownership-first lexical lookup chain exists once (the property-carrying chain is canonical; the algorithm-returning spelling is its projection, and the formerly duplicated algorithm-returning open-lookup chain is deleted). C# mirrors that structure: the independent plain implementations of resolved-builtin dispatch (including the duplicated if/while/repeat/atoms/range switch), dot-call dispatch, the lexical receiver-injection helpers, and the user/conditional/resolved/expression-position call family are deleted in favor of one shared value-projection helper over their counted twins; the evaluator's resolve-only lexical-lookup fast path is now the projection of the canonical binding-carrying lookup; and several already-dead plain wrappers were removed. The zero-argument property cache is unaffected in behavior — its key always collapsed the plain/counted access kinds to one access shape, so entries were shared across both spellings before and after; only internal per-kind instrumentation attribution moved onto the counted kinds. The async twin architecture, run-entry preparation, budgets and accounting chokepoints, diagnostics, spans, and all public entry points are unchanged. New Lean CoreTests guard families pin projection parity for the call, total-eval, and lookup families alongside the existing builtin and dot-call guards, and the exhaustive counted match makes a future AST variant a compile-time error until it is given a counted arm.
